title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + rope fused ops + rotary optimizations
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: reduce per-token latency and peak GPU memory for medium-to-long context LLM workloads by upgrading to FlashAttentionV2 kernels, exposing a fused QKV+ROPE path and rotary-embedding optimizations. This change replaces the older flash_attention_v1 kernels with vendor-optimized FlashAttentionV2 kernels where available, adds a fused-op implementation for QKV+ROPE that avoids intermediate buffers, and introduces a runtime feature flag to enable/disable rotary fusion per model. Changes include kernel implementations, runtime kernel selection heuristics (based on model dims and sequence length), unit and perf tests, and integration with the KV cache to support continuous batching and KV-prefetching. Benchmarks: internal perf runs show median per-token latency improvement of ~9% and p95 improvement of ~12% on A100 40GB for 32k-context models; VRAM usage reduced by ~18% for typical chat workloads due to elimination of intermediate Q/K/V buffers. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime config (attention.engine = "flashattn_v2") and model-level opt-in. Default remains backwards compatible; we will enable for select customers after canary. Risk/compatibility: fallback to legacy kernels when hardware or model ops are incompatible (e.g., unsupported CUDA/cuBLAS versions, int8 paths). Testing: new unit tests added, perf-canary job extended to run with representative prompt sets and to validate p95 SLOs. Operational notes: added metrics for fused-op hit rate and a tracing event to help debug KV cache interactions. Related linear items: ENG-2147 (attention kernel upgrade), ENG-2199 (continuous batching integration).

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice work on the fused QKV kernel. Two requests: (1) add a guard for older CUDA toolkit versions that may not support the warp-level intrinsics used here, and (2) can you include a small microbenchmark in perf harness to validate memory improvement?
Maya Thompson (author): Added CUDA version guard and updated perf harness to include VRAM measurement. Benchmarks attached to PR comment.

Priya Kapoor: Code looks good overall. Please make sure we have a clear fallback path for the int8/quantized runtime; previous PRs hit precision regressions when fusion was forced for quantized weights.
Maya Thompson (author): Quantized path now explicitly opts out of fused-rope by default; added a runtime toggle attention.engine.quantized_fusion = false. Added regression tests for int8 path.
Ethan Cole: Can we expose a metric for fused-op hit-rate so SRE can monitor canary toggles?
Maya Thompson (author): Added metrics.attention.fused_op_hit_rate and tracing event attention.fused_op.choice to help investigation.
ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (median -9% token latency, p95 -12%, mem -18%)
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV+ROPE path and rotary optimizations. Expect lower latency and reduced VRAM for compatible hardware. Feature is feature-gated and opt-in per model. See runtime.attention docs for rollout instructions.
notes_for_ops: Default kernel remains legacy; to enable for a deployment set runtime.attention.engine = "flashattn_v2" and ensure CUDA toolchain >= 12.2. Monitor metrics.attention.fused_op_hit_rate and perf SLOs after rollout.
backcompat_notes: Fallback to legacy kernels when FA2 is unavailable or when model uses quantized int8 paths. No model re-training required.
